title: First-order definability of regular tree languages
formal: Given a finite tree automaton, can one decide whether its language of finite ordered labeled trees is first-order definable using the standard tree and sibling-order relations, including the descendant relation?
context:
The intended signature is the ordered-tree/forest setting with descendant and sibling order. Results for restricted quantifier alternation do not give the full first-order characterization.

This short research proposal states the target identified in the September 2026 fundamental-problem search. The references give the source models and related results. A full self-contained formulation and detailed progress review remain to be written.

sentences: A finite tree automaton can recognize a collection of finite ordered labeled trees.
This project asks whether one can decide when that same collection is expressible in first-order logic with the specified tree and sibling-order relations.
The intended vocabulary includes descendant information, so changing to a more local signature changes the target.
Characterizations for restricted quantifier alternation address only portions of the requested logical language.
A complete test would explain which finite-state tree properties admit descriptions using quantification over individual nodes alone.
